title: Diagonal identities for 2-fibre products of fibred groupoids
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes [def-weil-size-convention]. Work with categories fibred in groupoids over $S$-schemes, functors over the base, natural isomorphisms over the base, and the object-and-isomorphism $2$-fibre products of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. The relative diagonal of $a:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ sends $x$ to $(x,x,\mathrm{id}_{a(x)})$. The following squares are $2$-cartesian (the comparison from the upper-left category to the $2$-fibre product of the other three is an equivalence over the base). (1) If $\mathcal X'=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Y'$ and $a':\mathcal X'\to\mathcal Y'$ is the projection, the square with horizontal arrows $\Delta_{a'}:\mathcal X'\to\mathcal X'\times_{\mathcal Y'}\mathcal X'$ and $\Delta_a:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$, and vertical arrows the projections induced by $\mathcal X'\to\mathcal X$, is $2$-cartesian. (2) For functors $u:\mathcal A\to\mathcal C$, $v:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$, $h:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, the square with upper row $i:\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal B\to\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal D}\mathcal B$, lower row $\Delta_h:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C\times_{\mathcal D}\mathcal C$, left map induced by $u$ on the first projection and right map induced by $(u,v)$, is $2$-cartesian; $i$ applies $h$ to the structural isomorphism. No stack, atlas, representability or finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 04YR (lemma-base-change-diagonal) and 04Z1 (lemma-fibre-product-after-map), fibrewise for fibred groupoids.

proof.text: Use the fibrewise triple model of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], with composition written right-to-left. For a base scheme $T$, all structural isomorphisms below lie over $1_T$. Write $b:\mathcal Y'\to\mathcal Y$ and $z=(x,y,\phi)$ in $\mathcal X'$, where $\phi:a(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}b(y)$. The right vertical functor in (1) sends $(z_1,z_2,\theta:y_1\xrightarrow{\sim}y_2)$ to $(x_1,x_2,\lambda)$, with $\lambda=\phi_2^{-1}b(\theta)\phi_1$. It respects arrows because their defining commuting squares imply the commuting square for $\lambda$; identities and composites are componentwise. It sends the relative diagonal to the relative diagonal strictly. In (2), the square is equipped with the natural isomorphism from $\Delta_hu$ to $(u,v)i$ whose components are $(1_{u(a)},\phi)$ at $(a,b,\phi)$. Its compatibility equation is $h(\phi)=h(\phi)h(1)$, and its naturality is exactly the defining arrow equation of $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal C}\mathcal B$. Thus both canonical comparison functors are defined over the base.

For (1), the fibre of the proposed pullback has objects $(x,z_1,z_2,\theta,r_1,r_2)$, where $r_j:x\xrightarrow{\sim}x_j$ and $a(r_2)=\lambda a(r_1)$. Its comparison $K_1$ sends $z=(x,y,\phi)$ to $(x,z,z,1_y,1_x,1_x)$. Given an arbitrary such object, put $z=(x,y_1,\phi_1a(r_1))$. The arrows $q_1=(r_1,1_{y_1}):z\to z_1$ and $q_2=(r_2,\theta):z\to z_2$ exist: the second arrow equation is $b(\theta)\phi_1a(r_1)=\phi_2a(r_2)$, which is the displayed relation after multiplying by $\phi_2$. The pair $(q_1,q_2)$ is an arrow from the diagonal of $z$ to $(z_1,z_2,\theta)$ since its two $\mathcal Y'$ components are $1$ and $\theta$. Together with $1_x$ it gives an isomorphism from $K_1(z)$ to the given pullback object, since its two projected components are $r_1,r_2$. This proves essential surjectivity in every fibre.

source.place: Tag 04YR, lemma-base-change-diagonal; objectwise expansion of the equivalences in its proof.

proof.text: For (1), a morphism $K_1(z)\to K_1(w)$ has an $\mathcal X$ component $s$ and two $\mathcal X'$ components $(p_1,t_1),(p_2,t_2)$. The diagonal compatibility in $\mathcal Y'$ forces $t_1=t_2=t$, and compatibility with the two identity comparison arrows in $\mathcal X$ forces $p_1=p_2=s$. The remaining equation is precisely $b(t)\phi_z=\phi_w a(s)$, so these data correspond bijectively to arrows $(s,t):z\to w$. Conversely each such arrow gives those components and satisfies every equation. Thus $K_1$ is fully faithful in every fibre, including all automorphisms.

source.place: Tag 04YR; arrow equations for the explicit comparison.

proof.text: For (2), put $Q=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal D}\mathcal B$. An object of $P=\mathcal C\times_{\mathcal C\times_{\mathcal D}\mathcal C}Q$ is $(c,a,b,\eta,\alpha,\beta)$ with $\eta:hu(a)\xrightarrow{\sim}hv(b)$, $\alpha:c\xrightarrow{\sim}u(a)$, $\beta:c\xrightarrow{\sim}v(b)$, and $\eta h(\alpha)=h(\beta)$. The comparison $K_2$ sends $(a,b,\phi)$ to $(u(a),a,b,h(\phi),1,\phi)$. Given an object of $P$, set $\phi=\beta\alpha^{-1}$; its defining equation gives $h(\phi)=\eta$. The components $\alpha^{-1}:u(a)\to c$ and the identity of $(a,b,\eta)$ in $Q$ define an isomorphism from $K_2(a,b,\phi)$ to the given object: its comparison equations are $\alpha\alpha^{-1}=1$ and $\beta\alpha^{-1}=\phi$. This proves essential surjectivity without any faithfulness assumption on $h$.

source.place: Tag 04Z1, lemma-fibre-product-after-map; supplies the omitted objectwise argument.

proof.text: For (2), a morphism between the canonical images of $(a,b,\phi)$ and $(a',b',\phi')$ consists of $t:u(a)\to u(a')$ and $(r:a\to a',s:b\to b')$ in $Q$. Compatibility with the first comparison component forces $t=u(r)$; the second says $v(s)\phi=\phi'u(r)$. This last equation is exactly the arrow condition over $\mathcal C$. It also implies the arrow condition over $\mathcal D$ after applying $h$, so imposes all the required conditions and no extra one. Conversely such $(r,s)$ supplies the unique $t$. Hence $K_2$ is fully faithful in every fibre.

source.place: Tag 04Z1; supplies the omitted arrowwise argument.

proof.text: The comparison functors are over $\mathit{Sch}/S$. Every arrow in a category fibred in groupoids is cartesian by the unique-factorization condition in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; hence these functors preserve cartesian arrows. The triple models are fibred in groupoids: lift each component over a base arrow and use the unique factorization property to lift the structural isomorphism; its inverse lifts likewise and the two composites are identities by uniqueness. The same componentwise uniqueness proves the cartesian property of the lifted pair. Work in the larger universe of [def-weil-size-convention] on the chosen small base and fibre categories. Apply [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-equivalence-criterion] to $K_1$ using steps 2--3, and to $K_2$ using steps 4--5. It gives quasi-inverses over the base and natural isomorphisms over base identities. These are exactly the two required $2$-cartesian assertions.

source.place: Tag 003Z, lemma-equivalence-fibred-categories; Tags 0040 and 02XI for the componentwise model.
